data.name: Salomaiah
data.gender_notes: Salomaiah is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Hebrew, Salomaiah means 'peaceful one of God'. In the Bible, it's a rare female name, possibly derived from the Hebrew word 'shalom' meaning 'peace'. The name Salomaiah carries the meaning “Peaceful, tranquil” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Salomaiah usually hope their child will grow to embody peaceful, tranquil and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes inner peace and calmness in spiritual life
data.etymology: Salomaiah belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Peaceful, tranquil.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Salomaiah total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

in_hebrew.name: שלמיה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם שלמיה מורכב מ'שלום' ו'אלוהים', ומשמעותו השלם האל או השלום מאלוהים. הוא נמצא בתנ'ך כדמות חשובה.

in_greek.name: Σαλωμαίας
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Σαλωμαίας προέρχεται από τα εβραϊκά και σημαίνει ειρήνη του Θεού. Στο Χριστιανισμό, το όνομα συνδέεται με την ειρήνη και την αρμονία που προσφέρει ο Θεός.

in_latin.name: Salomaiah
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Salomaiah derivatur ex hebraeo et significat pacem Dei. In traditione christiana, nomen hoc refertur ad pacem et harmoniam quam Deus praebet.

in_english.name: Salomaiah
in_english.meaning: Peace of God or Complete God
in_english.long_meaning: The name Salomaiah originates from Hebrew roots, combining 'shalom' (peace) and 'El' (God). It signifies the peace of God or completeness in God. While not directly mentioned in the New Testament, the name aligns with Christian values of peace and divine presence. Historically, names with similar roots have been used in Jewish and Christian traditions to express devotion and spiritual aspirations.

data.cultural_impact: Salomaiah is a name rooted in ancient Hebrew culture, reflecting the rich heritage of biblical traditions. Its use in Christianity represents a connection to the religious past, enabling individuals with this name to carry the weight of history and tradition. It is an intriguing and somewhat unique name for Christians in a global context.
data.spiritual_significance: Salomaiah's significance is deeply spiritual. The name underscores one's commitment to God, symbolizing a peaceful disposition and unwavering faith. Wearing this name can serve as a daily reminder to seek inner peace and harmony, allowing individuals to navigate life's ups and downs from a centered and grounded place.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Salomaiah may be seen as a name signifying the gentle and loving guidance of God (Salo) in the midst of sorrow and affliction (Maiah). It reminds us that even in our darkest moments, His presence brings comfort and hope.

biblical_reference.note: In the Bible, Salomaiah is mentioned as one of the signers of the covenant in Nehemiah 10:32.

historical_references.reference: In the 12th century, Salomaiah was the name of a character in the Old French epic poem, La Chanson de Roland.

modern_usage.modern_context: In today's world, the name Salomaiah continues to be cherished by Christian families globally. It is frequently featured on social media platforms where parents share their naming journeys, and Christian name websites where expectant parents research meaningful Biblical names. The name bridges traditional Christian values with modern faith identity, making it relevant for contemporary families seeking names with deep spiritual and Biblical significance.

name_in_real_life.story: Ruth Salomaiah, a minister in Athens, Greece, shares that their name Salomaiah meaning "Peaceful, tranquil" has been a constant source of inspiration, guiding them to serve others and live according to Christian values.
